title: PPA-Relevant Clustering-Driven Placement for Large-Scale VLSI Designs
problem: Place-and-route flows for large-scale designs face turnaround time and quality tradeoffs; scaling global placement to handle modern design complexity while maintaining solution quality is challenging.
motivation: Reducing P&R turnaround time while improving solution quality directly accelerates chip design productivity and enhances final chip performance metrics.
method: The paper uses PPA-aware clustering considering timing, power, and logical hierarchy to reduce netlist complexity and accelerate global placement. An ML-accelerated virtualized P&R methodology predicts optimal cluster shapes (aspect ratios and utilizations). The approach is validated on both open-source OpenROAD and commercial Cadence Innovus tools.
key_novelty: ML-driven prediction of optimal cluster shapes combined with PPA-aware netlist clustering to simultaneously improve placement turnaround time and post-route solution quality.
contributions: PPA-aware clustering methodology considering timing, power, and logical hierarchy during netlist clustering
ML-accelerated virtualized P&R for predicting optimal cluster shapes and utilizations
36-47% global placement runtime improvement with maintained HPWL on OpenROAD
Up to 90% TNS improvement and 3.92% power reduction on commercial tools
primary_theme: ML-driven PPA-aware clustering for VLSI placement acceleration
